Line 25 does `result = existing`, so when `existing` is omitted, `result` IS the shared default list, and the `result.append(...)` calls on lines 26-28 mutate it permanently. Consequently, results from earlier calls leak into later calls: `tag_orders(ORDERS, 'gift')` returns and stores `['o1','o3']` in the default; the subsequent call `tag_orders(ORDERS, 'rush')` appends 'o3' to that same list and returns `['o1','o3','o3']` instead of a fresh `['o3']`. This also contradicts the docstring, which promises a new list when `existing` is not given. (When `existing` IS passed explicitly, the caller's list is also mutated in place — same aliasing flaw.)

payload.rationale: The root cause is the classic mutable-default-argument bug: `existing: list = []` binds one shared list object at definition time, and `result = existing` aliases it, so every call without an explicit `existing` appends to the same persistent list, leaking results from earlier calls (e.g. `['o1','o3']` contaminating the 'rush' call to produce `['o1','o3','o3']`). The fix replaces the shared mutable default with a `None` sentinel and creates a fresh list per call when `existing` is omitted, exactly matching the docstring's promise of 'a new list otherwise'. When `existing` is passed explicitly, behavior is unchanged (the passed list is still appended to and returned), so `test_tag_orders_appends_to_existing` still passes.
